title: Benefits of Cloud Services

header.html: Describe the benefits of high availability and scalability in the cloud; Describe the benefits of reliability and predictability in the cloud; Describe the benefits of security and governance in the cloud; Describe the benefits of manageability in the cloud
the official AZ-900 study guide, skills measured as of July 20, 2026

html:
1The benefits at a glance

Benefit One-line meaning Key words in a question
High availability The service keeps running when parts fail uptime, SLA, failure, zones
Scalability Add or remove capacity to match demand peak, growth, demand
Reliability The system recovers from failure and keeps working resilient, self-healing, disaster recovery
Predictability Performance and cost can be foreseen forecast, consistent, budget
Security Built-in protection and compliance support threats, encryption, compliance
Governance Rules and standards applied to resources policy, standards, control
Manageability Easy to manage and monitor the resources automation, templates, portal

2High availability and scalability

High availability means the service is up when users need it. In the cloud you design with several copies of a resource in different places so one failure does not stop the service. Providers state targets in a service level agreement (SLA), for example 99.9% or 99.99% uptime. [Verify live] for current numbers.

Scalability means you can change capacity to match demand.

Type What it does Example
Vertical scaling (scale up) Make one resource bigger (more CPU or memory) Move a VM to a larger size
Horizontal scaling (scale out) Add more copies of the resource Add more VM instances behind a load balancer
Autoscaling Scale automatically by rules or schedule Add instances when CPU is high
Exam tip

. Scale up/down = bigger/smaller machine. Scale out/in = more/fewer machines. Elasticity (growing and shrinking automatically with demand) is why you pay only for what you need.

3Reliability and predictability

Reliability is the ability of a system to recover from failures and keep functioning. In Azure it is supported by:

  • Decentralized design: resources can be placed across datacenters, zones and regions (Module 4).
  • Backup and disaster recovery services.
  • Global footprint: a regional problem does not take down every region.

Predictability has two sides:

Side Meaning Tools
Performance predictability The app behaves consistently as demand changes autoscaling, load balancing
Cost predictability You can forecast and control spending pricing calculator, cost analysis, budgets (Module 11)
Exam tip

. Reliability = recover from failure; high availability = stay up. If the question says "recover" or "disaster", think reliability; if it says "uptime" or "SLA", think high availability.

4Security and governance

Security. The cloud provider secures the physical infrastructure, and the platform offers tools for you to secure your own part (identity, network controls, encryption, threat protection). The shared responsibility model (Module 1) decides who does what.

Governance. Cloud governance means applying rules and standards to resources: which regions and sizes are allowed, which tags are required, how access is granted. Azure helps with Azure Policy, resource locks, role-based access control and Microsoft Purview (Modules 9 and 12).

Compliance. Azure supports many compliance standards and has audit reports. [Verify live] The provider's certification does not make your own workload compliant: you must still configure it correctly.

Exam tip

. A common trap: "The provider is compliant, so my app is compliant." Wrong: compliance is shared.

5Manageability

Manageability has two parts in the study guide.

Part Meaning Examples
Management of the cloud Autoscaling, monitoring and alerts, templates and automation for the resources you run Azure Monitor, autoscale, ARM templates
Management in the cloud The ways you reach and administer resources Azure portal, CLI, PowerShell, REST APIs

Because resources are defined as code and managed through a common interface, you can deploy the same environment again and again with little manual work.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A web shop must handle a short rush of orders on one day, then return to normal. Which benefit lets it add capacity and release it afterward?

  • AGovernance
  • BPredictable pricing
  • CScalability and elasticity
  • DCompliance
Show the answer

Answer: C. Scalability, together with elasticity, allows capacity to grow and shrink with demand.

S2A team adds three more identical virtual machines behind a load balancer. What kind of scaling is this?

  • AVertical scaling (scale up)
  • BReducing the SLA
  • CHorizontal scaling (scale out)
  • DDisaster recovery
Show the answer

Answer: C. Adding more instances is scaling out (horizontal). Scaling up makes one machine larger.

S3An application keeps running when one datacenter in a region fails because copies run elsewhere. Which cloud benefit is shown?

  • AManageability
  • BHigh availability
  • CCost predictability
  • DServerless
Show the answer

Answer: B. High availability keeps the service running when part of the infrastructure fails.

S4A finance team wants to forecast monthly cloud spending and receive alerts when a budget is near. Which benefit is this?

  • AVertical scaling
  • BPredictability (cost)
  • CReliability
  • DCompliance
Show the answer

Answer: B. Cost predictability uses estimating and budgeting tools to forecast and control spending.

S5A company enforces that every resource must be created only in approved regions. Which benefit is this?

  • AGovernance
  • BElasticity
  • CHigh availability
  • DAutoscaling
Show the answer

Answer: A. Governance applies rules and standards, for example with Azure Policy.

S6An administrator deploys the same environment in three regions using a template. Which benefit is this?

  • AReliability only
  • BManageability
  • CCapEx
  • DPrivate cloud
Show the answer

Answer: B. Templates and automation make resources easy to deploy and manage the same way every time.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does an SLA state?

Show the answer

The uptime or performance target the provider commits to for a service.

R2Scale up or scale out: which adds more instances?

Show the answer

Scale out (horizontal).

R3Which benefit lets the system recover from failure and keep working?

Show the answer

Reliability.

R4Name the two sides of predictability.

Show the answer

Performance predictability and cost predictability.

R5What is governance in the cloud?

Show the answer

Applying rules and standards to resources, for example with Azure Policy.

R6Is a provider's compliance certificate enough to make your workload compliant?

Show the answer

No. Compliance is shared; you must configure your part correctly.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
High availability stays up through failures; stated by an SLA
Scalability scale up/down = bigger/smaller; scale out/in = more/fewer; autoscale by rules
Reliability recovers from failure; decentralized design, backup, disaster recovery
Predictability performance (autoscale, load balance) and cost (calculator, budgets)
Security provider secures the infrastructure; you secure identities, data, configuration
Governance rules and standards: Azure Policy, locks, RBAC, Purview
Manageability management of the cloud (autoscale, monitoring, templates) and in the cloud (portal, CLI, PowerShell, APIs)
